# Fetching packages with ezupdate

This page is for administrators who want a package from a package server on an installed site without downloading
and uploading it by hand. ezupdate reads the server's `index.xml`, shows what it offers next to what you have, and
fetches the archive straight into the local package repository. Installing it is then done on the kernel's package
pages.

![Updates and packages, Package servers](../../images/help/sp-servers.webp)

## Contents

1. [Open a server's packages](#open-a-servers-packages)
2. [The list](#the-list)
3. [Fetch a package](#fetch-a-package)
4. [Then install it](#then-install-it)
5. [From the command line](#from-the-command-line)
6. [Limits and errors](#limits-and-errors)

## Open a server's packages

On **Setup > Updates and packages > Package servers**, press **Packages** on a server's row: `/update/packages/<server>`.
Without a server name the first one, the built-in server of `package.ini`, is shown. Viewing needs `update/ezupdate`;
fetching needs `update/manage` (checked when you press the button, not only by hiding it).

## The list

The page "Packages on %server" shows every `<package>` of the server's `index.xml`, sorted by name:

| Column | From |
|---|---|
| Package | the `name` attribute (and `summary`) |
| Type | the `type` attribute: `site`, `contentclass`, `contentobject`, `sitestyle`, `extension` |
| Local copy | the version of the package of that name in the local repository (`eZPackage::getVersion()`), or none |
| Actions | **Fetch**, or **Fetch again** and **Open** (the local package's page, `/package/view/full/<name>`) when there is a local copy |

A **Filter** narrows the list as you type. "This server lists no packages, or its index.xml could not be read." means
the index was empty, unreachable or not a `<packages>` document.

## Fetch a package

1. Press **Fetch** on its row ("Fetching..." while it runs).
2. ezupdate downloads the archive from the `url` of the index entry and imports it with `eZPackage::import()`, the same
   import as the upload page, with the same archive checks.
3. The page says "The package %package %version is in the local package repository now."

**Fetch again** asks "Replace the local copy with the one from the server?" and then removes the local package before
it fetches. Removing the local copy does not uninstall what it installed.

The archive is written to a temporary file in the cache directory (`ezupdate/<name>.ezpkg`) and deleted after the
import. The package lands in the repository its `<vendor>` names, for the 7x packages `var/storage/packages/7x/`.

## Then install it

Fetching only imports. Open **Setup > Packages**, find the package (it is "Not installed" if it has install items),
open its page and press **Install** ([Installing and uninstalling](installing-and-uninstalling.md)). A site package
fetched this way is "Imported only": it is used by the setup wizard, the kickstarter or `exp:install`, for example for
an offline install, not installed from the package pages.

## From the command line

```bash
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php packages                    # the first server's packages
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php packages acme
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php fetch acme acme_site_democontent
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php fetch acme acme_site_democontent --replace
```

`fetch <server> <package> [--replace]` "download[s] a .ezpkg into the local package repository"; `--replace` replaces a
package already there. Then install with `php ezpm.php install <name>` or on the package's page.

## Limits and errors

From `extension/ezupdate/classes/ezupdatepackageservers.php`:

| Check | Limit |
|---|---|
| Transport | the PHP curl extension, HTTPS only, also for redirects (at most 5) |
| `index.xml` | at most 1 MiB, root element `<packages>` |
| archive | at most 256 MiB; its `url` must be `https://` |
| time | 15 seconds to connect, 300 seconds in all |
| proxy | `site.ini [ProxySettings] ProxyServer` when set |

| Message | Means |
|---|---|
| "The package is already in the local repository." | use **Fetch again** or `--replace` |
| "The server does not offer this package." | the name is not in the server's index |
| "The package address must be an https:// URL." | the index entry's `url` is not HTTPS |
| "Could not fetch %url: %reason" | the download failed; the reason is curl's |
| "The server did not answer with a package index." | `index.xml` is not a `<packages>` document |
| "The file is not a valid package." | the import refused the archive |
| "The PHP curl extension is needed to reach a server." | install or enable `curl` for PHP |
